title: WIP: Add Zookeeper Protocol Dissector
description:
This adds a new dissector for the protocols used by Zookeeper.

Zookeeper is a distributed database focused on maintaining consistent
configuration information, even in the presence of network partitions
(split brain). For more info, see https://zookeeper.apache.org/

Zookeeper uses three different protocols:
1. The client protocol, used by clients to communicate with the
zookeeper cluster. Defaults to port `2181`.
2. The inter-cluster protocol, used by the servers within the cluster to
stay in-sync with each other. Defaults to port `2888`.
3. The special leader election protocol, used by servers within the
cluster for electing a new leader when a network partition happens. Defaults to port `3888`.

This PR only adds support for the client protocol.

The initial template was generated using:
```
./generate-dissector.py \
--name "Jeff Widman" \
--email "“jeff@jeffwidman.com" \
--protoname "Zookeeper Protocol" \
--protoshortname "Zookeeper" \
--protoabbrev "zookeeper" \
-f
```

I wasn't sure what to use for the `protoname`/`protoshortname`/`protoabbrev` values given that there are three(!) different protocols used by Zookeeper (see PR description for details).

On the one hand, it's cleanest to keep client protocol separate from server protocol (which in turn consists of both the communication protocol and the leader-election protocol). On the other hand, most users will immediately look for the "zookeeper protocol" and not even consider there might be an inter-cluster protocol... ie, in their minds, the zookeeper protocol _is_ the client protocol. 

I've actually never looked into the inter-cluster / server-side zookeeper protocol.. perhaps there are message re-use conflicts that prevent using a single dissector for both the client protocol and the server protocol, but I doubt it. I also wasn't sure what the wireshark standard was... as this can't be the first time this issue of whether to handle client/server protocols within a single dissector or separate dissectors has arisen.

Any input?

+/* Register the protocol with Wireshark.

+{

+        /* Use create_dissector_handle() to indicate that
+         * dissect_zookeeper() returns the number of bytes it dissected (or 0
+         * if it thinks the packet does not belong to Zookeeper Client Protocol).
+         */
+        zookeeper_handle = create_dissector_handle(dissect_zookeeper,
+                                                   proto_zookeeper);
+        initialized = TRUE;
+    }
+    else
+    {
+        /* If you perform registration functions which are dependent upon
+         * prefs then you should de-register everything which was associated
+         * with the previous settings and re-register using the new prefs
+         * settings here. In general this means you need to keep track of
+         * the zookeeper_handle and the value the preference had at the time
+         * you registered.  The zookeeper_handle value and the value of the
+         * preference can be saved using local statics in this
+         * function (proto_reg_handoff).
+         */
+        dissector_delete_uint("tcp.port", current_port, zookeeper_handle);
+    }
+
+    current_port = tcp_port_pref;
+
+    dissector_add_uint("tcp.port", current_port, zookeeper_handle);
+    // TODO add the other two protocols here later:
+    // 1. Zookeeper Atomic Broadcast (ZAB) internal consensus protocol
+    // 2. Zookeeper Leader Election protocol
+}
+
+#if 0
+
+/* Simpler form of proto_reg_handoff_zookeeper which can be used if there are
+ * no prefs-dependent registration function calls. */
+void
+proto_reg_handoff_zookeeper(void)
+{
+    dissector_handle_t zookeeper_handle;
+
+    /* Use create_dissector_handle() to indicate that dissect_zookeeper()
+     * returns the number of bytes it dissected (or 0 if it thinks the packet
+     * does not belong to Zookeeper Client Protocol).
+     */
+    zookeeper_handle = create_dissector_handle(dissect_zookeeper,
+            proto_zookeeper);
+    dissector_add_uint_with_preference("tcp.port", zookeeper_TCP_PORT, zookeeper_handle);
+}
+#endif

commits_data.title: Add Zookeeper (Client) Protocol Dissector
commits_data.message:
Add Zookeeper (Client) Protocol Dissector

This adds a new dissector for the protocols used by Zookeeper.

Zookeeper is a distributed database focused on maintaining consistent
configuration information, even in the presence of network partitions
(split brain). For more info, see https://zookeeper.apache.org/

Zookeeper uses three different protocols:
1. The client protocol, used by clients to communicate with the
zookeeper cluster. Defaults to port `2181`.
2. The inter-cluster protocol, used by the servers within the cluster to
stay in-sync with each other. Defaults to port `2888`.
3. The special leader election protocol, used by servers within the
cluster for electing a new leader. Defaults to port `3888`.

This PR only adds support for the client protocol.
